name: Let a guardian ask to meet a teacher about their own child, and have the teacher offer a slot from their own free time
priorityReason: The everyday case, arising whenever a family is concerned about something. It needs no window, no coordinator and no slot grid.

goal.outcome: the meeting happens without an event being organised around it, and what was said is on the child's record

dataFields.name: Free slots
dataFields.validation: The slots in which the teacher is genuinely free, read from the timetable and excluding teaching, substitute cover and approved leave (BR-2).

businessRules.rule: A guardian requests a meeting with a teacher who teaches their own child. A teacher who does not teach the child cannot be requested, and a child who is not theirs cannot be selected.

The system offers the teacher the slots in which they are genuinely free, read from the published timetable and excluding any period in which they are teaching, are covering another class as a substitute, or are on approved leave. A slot offered in any of those three is a meeting that will not happen.

The teacher chooses the slot, not the guardian. The guardian may state a preference, and the teacher meets it where they can. This is what distinguishes an on-demand meeting from the school-wide event, where the guardian chooses from a grid.
The teacher may propose a slot outside timetabled hours where the school allows meetings after school.
A decline carries a reason, and the guardian is told it. A request that goes unanswered, or is refused with no explanation, is worse than one declined plainly.
Either side may cancel before the meeting. The slot is released, the other side is told, and the request may be raised again.

After the meeting the teacher records that it took place and any note arising. The note is held against the student and is visible to the coordinator, so a pattern of concerns about one child is visible to somebody above the classroom.

No coordinator is required for any of this to proceed. The coordinator sees what is happening in their sections; they do not approve it. Requiring them would make an everyday conversation into an event.
There is no window, no slot grid and no opening or closing date. This is the everyday case and any of those would be scaffolding around a conversation.

A confirmed slot that later becomes unavailable — because the teacher's leave is approved, or their timetable changes — is released and both sides are told, rather than the meeting standing against a slot the teacher is no longer free in.
A request is never deleted. A declined or cancelled request stays on the record, so a family who asked three times and was declined three times is visible.

basicFlow.userAction: Selects their child and a teacher who teaches them, writes a short reason and gives any timing preference.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Offers only teachers of that child, and records the request against the student.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens the request and reads the reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Notifies the teacher and shows the reason and the preference.
Offers the slots in which the teacher is genuinely free, read from the timetable and excluding teaching, substitute cover and approved leave.

basicFlow.navigation: Offer a slot → Select a free slot → Confirm
basicFlow.userAction: Selects a slot and confirms it, meeting the guardian's preference where they can.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Confirms the meeting on a slot the teacher chose.
Tells the guardian the confirmed slot, or the decline and its reason.

basicFlow.userAction: Cancels before the meeting where either side must.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Releases the slot, tells the other side, and leaves the request able to be raised again.

basicFlow.navigation: Communication → My meetings → Record that it took place
basicFlow.userAction: Records that the meeting took place and any note arising.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Holds the note against the student, visible to the coordinator.

alternateFlows.condition: The teacher cannot meet the request
alternateFlows.navigation: Meeting requests → Decline with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: The reason is recorded and the guardian is told it. A request refused with no explanation is worse than one declined plainly (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: The teacher has no free slot in timetabled hours
alternateFlows.navigation: Offer a slot → Propose a slot outside timetabled hours
alternateFlows.behaviour: They propose a time after school where the school allows meetings then (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The teacher is on approved leave that week
alternateFlows.behaviour: Those slots are not offered at all, since a slot offered during leave is a meeting that will not happen (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: A confirmed slot later becomes unavailable
alternateFlows.behaviour: The slot is released and both sides are told, rather than the meeting standing against a slot the teacher is no longer free in (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian cancels and wants to ask again
alternateFlows.behaviour: A fresh request is raised. The cancelled one stays on the record (BR-6, BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: The coordinator reviews what is happening in their sections
alternateFlows.behaviour: They see the requests, the meetings and the notes without being required for any of them to proceed (BR-8).

alternateFlows.navigation: My meetings → Record that it did not take place
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is recorded as not having happened, so a family who repeatedly does not attend is visible.

departures.requirement: There is no window, no slot grid, no opening or closing date and no coordinator approval anywhere in this flow. Each would turn an everyday conversation into an event.
A slot is offered only where the teacher is not teaching, not covering and not on leave. A slot offered in any of those three is a meeting that will not happen.
A guardian is told the outcome whether the request is confirmed or declined, and a decline always carries a reason.
A guardian can request a meeting and read the outcome on a phone.
Requests and their notes are retained for the academic session and 3 years afterwards, since a note about a child is part of their record.

openQuestions.question: Does the school allow meetings outside timetabled hours, and within what times?
openQuestions.assumption: Permitted as modelled where the school allows it. The hours are not specified.

openQuestions.question: How long is a meeting slot, and does it occupy a whole free period?
openQuestions.assumption: A whole free period as modelled. Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Is there a limit on how many meetings one guardian may request in a term?
openQuestions.assumption: None as modelled. A family requesting weekly is the case to consider.

openQuestions.question: Should the guardian see the note the teacher recorded, or is it internal?
openQuestions.assumption: Internal as modelled, visible to the coordinator only.

openQuestions.question: May a guardian request a meeting with the class incharge about a subject teacher's class?
openQuestions.assumption: Not as modelled; the request goes to a teacher of the child.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
